text.p: Mazda Motor of America said Monday it was surprised and dismayed to learn that it was being sued by 14 states over allegations of false and deceptive advertising in its auto leasing program.
A Mazda spokesman said the company had only heard about the lawsuits from the media, not from the offices of the 14 attorneys general.

"This thing came literally out of the blue," spokesman Jay Amestoy told Reuters. "We are at a loss to understand why we're being singled out when our practices are in line with the rest of the industry."

Amestoy said Mazda was particularly dismayed since it believed automotive leasing and its promotion were regulated at the federal level. He said Mazda thought it was complying with all such federal regulations.

"Up until now, we had been in discussion with various attorneys general as well as officials from the federal Trade Commission and had every reason to believe that we would reach an amicable agreement," Amestoy said.
The states filing lawsuits against Mazda comprised Minnesota, Missouri, California, Connecticut, Arizona, Iowa, Massachusetts, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Maryland, Washington, Nevada, and Ohio.
Amestoy said that since Mazda was not given an opportunity to see the lawsuits, it could not offer any additional comment on the specific allegations.
But he countered the statement made by Washington Attorney General Christine Gregoire, who said the states had attempted to settle without a lawsuit but Mazda was not responsive.
"Absolutely not true. We have been in discussions all along," Amestoy said.

The lawsuits allege that Mazda required consumers to pay up-front fees of up to $900 to get the advertised "zero down" or "penny down" lease. The up-front fees include a security deposit and the first month's lease, payment and in some cases a $450 acquisition fee.
The states said the advertising campaign ran from March through June, 1996. Amestoy said the campaign was handled by Foote, Cone and Belding.
Mazda is 33.4 percent-owned by Ford Motor Co.
